000509:       function _livestockDialogueHeadWorldPosition(animal, kind, out = new THREE.Vector3()) {
000510:         const frame = window.AnimalChatheadFrame?.frameForKind?.(kind);
000511:         const plane = animal?.avatarRef?.frontPlane || null;
000512:         const modelWidth = Number(animal?.modelWidth);
000513:         const modelHeight = Number(animal?.modelHeight);
000514:         if (frame && plane?.localToWorld && Number.isFinite(modelWidth) && Number.isFinite(modelHeight)) {
000515:           const centerX = frame.x + frame.width * 0.5;
000516:           const centerY = frame.y + frame.height * 0.5;
000517:           out.set(
000518:             (centerX - 0.5) * modelWidth,
000519:             (0.5 - centerY) * modelHeight,
000520:             0,
000521:           );
000522:           plane.updateWorldMatrix?.(true, false);
000523:           return plane.localToWorld(out);
000524:         }
000525:         if (animal?.avatarRef?.group?.getWorldPosition) {
000526:           animal.avatarRef.group.getWorldPosition(out);
000527:           out.y += (Number.isFinite(modelHeight) ? modelHeight : 1) * 0.25;
000528:         }
000529:         return out;
000530:       }

000532:       function createLivestockNpcDialogueAdapter(animal, livestockRec, kind, dialogueLines = []) {
000533:         const avatarRef = animal.avatarRef;
000534:         const headScratch = new THREE.Vector3();
000535:         return {
000536:           rec: {
000537:             id: `livestock:${livestockRec.id}`,
000538:             name: livestockRec.name || 'Livestock',
000539:             dialogueLines: Array.isArray(dialogueLines) && dialogueLines.length ? dialogueLines : ['...'],
000540:           },
000541:           // Deliberately no `profile`: triggered livestock dialogue stays in 3D.
000542:           // Authored animal crops are rendered only by popup/ambient chatheads;
000543:           // full dialogue uses the frame center strictly as head-position metadata.
000544:           root: avatarRef?.group,
000545:           avatarHeight: Number(animal.modelHeight) || 1,
000546:           pause: 0,
000547: 
000548:           applyFacingDeadzone(targetRot, lerp) {
000549:             const blend = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, Number(lerp) || 0));
000550:             const current = Number.isFinite(animal.groupRot) ? animal.groupRot : (avatarRef?.group?.rotation?.y || 0);
000551:             animal.groupRot = current + angleDiff(targetRot, current) * blend;
000552:             animal.targetRot = targetRot;
000553:             if (avatarRef?.group) avatarRef.group.rotation.y = animal.groupRot;
000554:             return animal.groupRot;
000555:           },
000556: 
000557:           dialogueHeadWorldPosition(out = new THREE.Vector3()) {
000558:             return _livestockDialogueHeadWorldPosition(animal, kind, out);
000559:           },
000560: 
000561:           applyDialogueEyeContact(targetWorld, dt) {
000562:             if (!targetWorld || !avatarRef) return false;
000563:             const selfHead = _livestockDialogueHeadWorldPosition(animal, kind, headScratch);
000564:             const dx = targetWorld.x - selfHead.x;
000565:             const dy = targetWorld.y - selfHead.y;
000566:             const dz = targetWorld.z - selfHead.z;
000567:             const horizontal = Math.hypot(dx, dz);
000568:             if (horizontal < 1e-6 && Math.abs(dy) < 1e-6) return false;
000569:             const desiredWorldRot = -Math.atan2(dz, dx) + Math.PI / 2;
000570:             const bodyRot = Number.isFinite(animal.groupRot) ? animal.groupRot : (avatarRef.group?.rotation?.y || 0);
000571:             const yawDeg = angleDiff(desiredWorldRot, bodyRot) * 180 / Math.PI;
000572:             const pitchDeg = -Math.atan2(dy, Math.max(0.0001, horizontal)) * 180 / Math.PI;
000573:             avatarRef.updateHeadYaw?.(yawDeg, Math.max(0, Number(dt) || 0));
000574:             avatarRef.updateHeadRotation?.(pitchDeg, Math.max(0, Number(dt) || 0));
000575:             return true;
000576:           },
000577:         };
000578:       }

000587:           if (cleaned) return;
000588:           cleaned = true;
000589:           animal._dialogueFrozen = false;
000590:           animal.avatarRef?.updateHeadYaw?.(0, 1);
000591:           animal.avatarRef?.setHeadRotation?.(0);
000592:         };
000593:         try {
000594:           await openNpcDialogue(walker, {
000595:             skipNpcMeta: true,
000596:             recordMemory: false,
000597:           });
000598:           return true;

018553:       // Snaps the camera's follow target to the player's current position,
018554:       // including ground height — exterior zones now carry real per-tile

018557:       // assuming a flat Y=0 ground plane, or a player standing on an elevated

018568:       function portraitAvatarCenterWorldPosition(root) {
018569:         let avatarRoot = null;
018570:         root?.traverse?.(child => {
018571:           if (!avatarRoot && Number.isFinite(child.userData?.portraitModelHeight)) avatarRoot = child;
018572:         });
018573:         if (!avatarRoot) return null;
018574:         const center = new THREE.Vector3();
018575:         avatarRoot.updateWorldMatrix?.(true, false);
018576:         avatarRoot.getWorldPosition(center);
018577:         const height = avatarRoot.userData.portraitModelHeight;
018578:         const placementRatio = avatarRoot.userData.portraitVerticalPlacementRatio ?? 0.5;
018579:         center.y += (placementRatio - 0.5) * height;
018580:         return center;
018581:       }

018583:       // Cutscene dialogue's stand-in for a "player" anchor: the real
018584:       // dialoguePortraitCameraAim below hardcodes the actual player mesh as
018585:       // one of its two portrait-center anchors, which is meaningless here
018586:       // (neither cutscene speaker is ever the real player, who may be
018587:       // sitting untouched somewhere else entirely in the save). Pins the
018588:       // shot to the SPEAKING actor's own visual center instead — a
018589:       // creature's avatarRef.group already sits at its own body-center
018590:       // height (see cutscenePreviewApplyState), while an NPC/player's
018591:       // coin-plane needs the same portrait-tagged-child lookup real
018592:       // gameplay uses. Returns null (falling back to the generic elevated
018593:       // follow-camera framing) for a freeform placeholder actor, which has
018594:       // neither.
018595:       function cutscenePreviewSpeakerCenterY(entity) {

018597:         if (entity.kind === 'creature') return entity.root?.position.y ?? null;

018601:       function dialoguePortraitCameraAim(modeCfg, tx, tz, distance, baseAngle) {
018602:         if (!modeCfg.alignToDialoguePortraitCenters) return null;
018603:         if (cutscenePreviewActive) {
018604:           const y = cutscenePreviewSpeakerCenterY(cutscenePreviewDialogueSpeaker);
018605:           return y == null ? null : { cameraY: y, lookY: y, targetX: tx, targetZ: tz };
018606:         }
018607:         if (!_dialogueWalker?.root) return null;
018608:         const hasAuthoredSpeakerHead = typeof _dialogueWalker.dialogueHeadWorldPosition === 'function';
018609:         const npcCenter = hasAuthoredSpeakerHead
018610:           ? _dialogueWalker.dialogueHeadWorldPosition(new THREE.Vector3())
018611:           : portraitAvatarCenterWorldPosition(_dialogueWalker.root);
018612:         if (!npcCenter) return null;
018613: 
018614:         // Animal-shaped dialogue speakers provide an authored head point rather than
018615:         // an NPC portrait center. Treat that exact world-space pixel as the normal
018616:         // npcDialogue camera target: same configured distance/angle/azimuth/zoom,
018617:         // but no player->speaker pitch extrapolation (which can aim below terrain
018618:         // when the speaker is much shorter than the player).
018619:         if (hasAuthoredSpeakerHead) {
018620:           return {
018621:             cameraY: npcCenter.y + Math.sin(baseAngle) * distance,
018622:             lookY: npcCenter.y,
018623:             targetX: npcCenter.x,
018624:             targetZ: npcCenter.z,
018625:           };
018626:         }
018627: 
018628:         const playerCenter = portraitAvatarCenterWorldPosition(playerMesh);
018629:         if (!playerCenter) return null;
018630:         const minDistance = modeCfg.portraitCenterMinDistanceTiles ?? 0.001;
018631:         const portraitDistance = Math.max(
018632:           minDistance,
018633:           Math.hypot(npcCenter.x - playerCenter.x, npcCenter.z - playerCenter.z),
018634:         );
018635:         const rawPortraitPitch = Math.atan2(npcCenter.y - playerCenter.y, portraitDistance);
018636:         const maxUpwardPitch = THREE.MathUtils.degToRad(modeCfg.maxUpwardPortraitPitchDeg ?? 0);
018637:         const portraitPitch = Math.min(rawPortraitPitch, maxUpwardPitch);
018638:         const cameraY = rawPortraitPitch > maxUpwardPitch
018639:           ? (playerCenter.y + npcCenter.y) / 2
018640:           : playerCenter.y;
018641:         const cameraHorizontalDistance = Math.cos(baseAngle) * distance;
018642:         return {
018643:           cameraY,
018644:           lookY: cameraY + Math.tan(portraitPitch) * cameraHorizontalDistance,
018645:           targetX: tx,
018646:           targetZ: tz,
018647:         };
018648:       }

018650:       // Every mesh worth pulling the camera in front of, for whatever area is
018651:       // currently active. Zones keep their existing tagged-mesh collection
018652:       // (buildZoneScene's `occlusionMeshes`, built once per zone from
018653:       // `.userData.cameraObstacle` tags on cliff/mesa skins) as a base, but

018661:       // for losing sight of animals behind them; furniture matters for the
018662:       // seated camera specifically, since a chair can easily have another
018663:       // piece of furniture right behind it) — so those are gathered fresh
018664:       // each call instead. Cheap in practice: a handful of structures/
018665:       // furniture pieces at most, and this only runs once a frame.
018666:       function currentAreaOcclusionMeshes() {

018671:         }
018672:         const meshes = [];

018674:         // same tagged-mesh snapshot as zones, collected once when the
018675:         // building's scene is built (see loadBuildingScene). Without this,
018676:         // a den's carved cavern rock (or any other building's walls) never
018677:         // pulled the camera in when it got between the camera and the
018678:         // player, unlike the outdoor case just above.

018680:           for (const m of (_buildingScenes.get(currentArea)?.occlusionMeshes || [])) meshes.push(m);
018681:         }

018684:           for (const entry of farmBuildings) if (entry._mesh) meshes.push(entry._mesh);
018685:         }
018686:         if (currentArea === 'town') {
018687:           for (const entry of _townBuildingGroups) if (entry.group) meshes.push(entry.group);
018688:         }
018689:         if (currentArea === 'interior' && activeCameraMode === 'seated' && interiorWallGroup) meshes.push(interiorWallGroup);

018682:         if (currentArea === 'farm') {

018684:           for (const entry of farmBuildings) if (entry._mesh) meshes.push(entry._mesh);
018685:         }

018688:         }
018689:         if (currentArea === 'interior' && activeCameraMode === 'seated' && interiorWallGroup) meshes.push(interiorWallGroup);
018690:         for (const obj of interiorFurnitureObjects) {
018691:           const isActiveSeat = sitInteraction && obj.area === currentArea
018692:             && obj.key === sitInteraction.furnitureKey && obj.col === sitInteraction.col && obj.row === sitInteraction.row;
018693:           if (obj.area === currentArea && obj.mesh && !isActiveSeat) meshes.push(obj.mesh);

018697:       // Pulls the camera in along the target→camera line if something from
018698:       // currentAreaOcclusionMeshes() sits between them — the fixed south-of-
018699:       // player follow camera has no other way to keep the player visible
018700:       // once something tall is in that gap, since generation alone can bias
018701:       // terrain but can't guarantee a clear line at this camera's shallow
018702:       // angle (see conversation history: even a single-tier rise close to
018703:       // the player already eats most of the vertical slack a ~14-tile,
018704:       // ~33°-elevation sightline allows).
018705:       const CAMERA_FLOOR_CLEARANCE = 0.2; // minimum height above ground the camera is ever allowed to settle at (see the floor guard below)
018706:       const SEATED_CAMERA_WALL_CLEARANCE = 0.25; // gap kept between a seated camera and the detected wall face (used by occlusionSafeCameraPosition)
018707:       const SEATED_CAMERA_MIN_DISTANCE = 0.04; // emergency near-target limit used when a chair is almost flush against a wall
018708:       const SEATED_CAMERA_MIN_FRAMING_DISTANCE = 0.8; // closest useful third-person framing distance before the camera searches sideways for room
018709:       let _seatedOcclusionDistance = null; // smoothed seated-camera distance used while an obstruction clears
018710:       let _seatedOcclusionUpdatedAt = 0; // previous seated occlusion update time used to calculate smoothing delta
018711:       let _seatedCameraDebug = null; // latest seated obstruction solve, exposed to Pixel Probe for mobile diagnosis
018712:       function occlusionSafeCameraPosition(lookAtX, lookAtY, lookAtZ, idealX, idealY, idealZ) {
018713:         let resultX = idealX, resultY = idealY, resultZ = idealZ;
018714:         const obstacles = currentAreaOcclusionMeshes();
018715:         const dx = idealX - lookAtX, dy = idealY - lookAtY, dz = idealZ - lookAtZ;
018716:         const dist = Math.hypot(dx, dy, dz);
018717:         if (dist >= 0.5) {
018718:           let dir = { x: dx / dist, y: dy / dist, z: dz / dist };
018719:           let desiredSafeDist = dist;
018720:           let directHitDistance = null;
018721:           let chosenSideOffsetDeg = 0;
018722:           if (obstacles && obstacles.length) {
018723:             _cameraOcclusionRaycaster.set(new THREE.Vector3(lookAtX, lookAtY, lookAtZ), new THREE.Vector3(dir.x, dir.y, dir.z));
018724:             // A chair can put the seated target much closer than 0.3 tiles to
018725:             // a wall. Use a short near plane there so the wall is not skipped;
018726:             // ordinary standing cameras retain the player-avoidance distance.
018727:             _cameraOcclusionRaycaster.near = activeCameraMode === 'seated' ? 0.02 : 0.3;
018728:             _cameraOcclusionRaycaster.far = dist;
018729:             // recursive:true — zone occlusion meshes are already individual
018730:             // tagged leaf meshes (harmless either way there), but the
018731:             // house/barn/furniture entries above are whole Groups.
018732:             const hits = _cameraOcclusionRaycaster.intersectObjects(obstacles, true);
018733:             if (hits.length) {
018734:               directHitDistance = hits[0].distance;
018735:               if (activeCameraMode === 'seated') {
018736:                 // Never impose a minimum that lies beyond the wall. The old
018737:                 // 0.85-tile minimum did exactly that for wall-backed chairs,
018738:                 // leaving the camera embedded despite a correct ray hit.
018739:                 desiredSafeDist = Math.min(dist, Math.max(
018740:                   SEATED_CAMERA_MIN_DISTANCE,
018741:                   hits[0].distance - SEATED_CAMERA_WALL_CLEARANCE,
018742:                 ));
018743: 
018744:                 // If the wall leaves too little room to frame the seated
018745:                 // avatar, collapsing to the target makes the avatar clip the
018746:                 // near plane. Search progressively around the chair instead;
018747:                 // this produces an over-the-shoulder slide along the wall
018748:                 // while preserving the user's pitch and target.
018749:                 if (desiredSafeDist < SEATED_CAMERA_MIN_FRAMING_DISTANCE) {
018750:                   let best = { dir, safeDist: desiredSafeDist, offsetDeg: 0 };
018751:                   for (const offsetDeg of [25, -25, 45, -45, 70, -70, 90, -90]) {
018752:                     const a = THREE.MathUtils.degToRad(offsetDeg);
018753:                     const candidateDir = {
018754:                       x: dir.x * Math.cos(a) + dir.z * Math.sin(a),
018755:                       y: dir.y,
018756:                       z: -dir.x * Math.sin(a) + dir.z * Math.cos(a),
018757:                     };
018758:                     _cameraOcclusionRaycaster.set(
018759:                       new THREE.Vector3(lookAtX, lookAtY, lookAtZ),
018760:                       new THREE.Vector3(candidateDir.x, candidateDir.y, candidateDir.z),
018761:                     );
018762:                     _cameraOcclusionRaycaster.near = 0.02;
018763:                     _cameraOcclusionRaycaster.far = dist;
018764:                     const candidateHits = _cameraOcclusionRaycaster.intersectObjects(obstacles, true);
018765:                     const candidateSafeDist = candidateHits.length
018766:                       ? Math.max(SEATED_CAMERA_MIN_DISTANCE, candidateHits[0].distance - SEATED_CAMERA_WALL_CLEARANCE)
018767:                       : dist;
018768:                     if (candidateSafeDist > best.safeDist) best = { dir: candidateDir, safeDist: candidateSafeDist, offsetDeg };
018769:                     if (best.safeDist >= dist - 1e-4) break;
018770:                   }
018771:                   dir = best.dir;
018772:                   desiredSafeDist = Math.min(dist, best.safeDist);
018773:                   chosenSideOffsetDeg = best.offsetDeg;
018774:                 }
018775:               } else {
018776:                 desiredSafeDist = Math.min(dist, Math.max(3, hits[0].distance - 0.6));
018777:               }
018778:             }
018779:           }
018780:           let safeDist = desiredSafeDist;
018781:           if (activeCameraMode === 'seated') {
018782:             // Smooth toward the freshly raycast distance every frame. The old
018783:             // direct assignment made the camera stick to whichever wall face
018784:             // happened to win one raycast, then snap when that face changed.
018785:             const now = performance.now();
018786:             const dt = _seatedOcclusionUpdatedAt ? Math.min(0.1, (now - _seatedOcclusionUpdatedAt) / 1000) : 0;
018787:             _seatedOcclusionUpdatedAt = now;
018788:             if (_seatedOcclusionDistance == null) _seatedOcclusionDistance = desiredSafeDist;
018789:             if (desiredSafeDist < _seatedOcclusionDistance) {
018790:               // Pull in immediately so no frame can remain inside a newly
018791:               // detected wall. Only the unobstructed move back out is eased.
018792:               _seatedOcclusionDistance = desiredSafeDist;
018793:             } else {
018794:               const alpha = 1 - Math.exp(-8 * dt);
018795:               _seatedOcclusionDistance += (desiredSafeDist - _seatedOcclusionDistance) * alpha;
018796:             }
018797:             safeDist = clamp(_seatedOcclusionDistance, SEATED_CAMERA_MIN_DISTANCE, dist);
018798:             _seatedCameraDebug = {
018799:               idealDistance: dist,
018800:               directHitDistance,
018801:               desiredDistance: desiredSafeDist,

018851:         return { x: resultX, y: resultY, z: resultZ };

018853: 
018854:       // How far under a tree canopy's own recorded influence radius the player
018855:       // has to be before manual zoom-out gets hard-limited to its underside
018856:       // height — ports the standalone foliage tool's camera-vs-canopy
018857:       // obstruction concept (see buildZoneScene's canopyZones / the
018858:       // vegGroup.userData.canopyClamp tagging in _buildZoneFloorMeshes).
018859:       // Only ever raises the effective zoom used for THIS frame's distance —
018860:       // never mutates s_zoomScale itself, so the player's own wheel/slider
018861:       // setting is restored the instant they step out of every canopy's radius.
018862:       function canopyZoomFloor(tx, tz, lookY) {
018863:         if (!_isZoneArea(currentArea)) return 0;
018864:         const zones = _zoneScenes.get(currentArea)?.canopyZones;
018865:         if (!zones || !zones.length) return 0;
018866:         const modeCfg = cameraModeConfig(activeCameraMode);
018867:         const angle = THREE.MathUtils.degToRad((modeCfg.angleFromGroundDeg ?? 32.73) + cameraAngleOffsetDeg);
018868:         const distanceTiles = modeCfg.distanceTiles ?? 14;
018869:         const sinAngle = Math.sin(angle);
018870:         const CANOPY_CLEARANCE = 0.3;
018871:         let floor = 0;
018872:         for (const z of zones) {
018873:           const dx = tx - z.x, dz = tz - z.z;
018874:           if (dx * dx + dz * dz > z.radius * z.radius) continue;
018875:           const headroom = z.undersideY - CANOPY_CLEARANCE - lookY;
018876:           const required = headroom > 1e-4 ? (sinAngle * distanceTiles) / headroom : Infinity;
018877:           if (required > floor) floor = required;
018878:         }
018879:         return floor;
018880:       }
018881:       function updateCameraPosition() {
018882:         const modeCfg = cameraModeConfig(activeCameraMode);
018883:         // A cutscene Zoom card's percent (100 = the captured shot's own
018884:         // unmodified framing, higher = closer) — entirely separate from the
018885:         // player's own s_zoomScale wheel setting so it never leaks into
018886:         // normal gameplay once the cutscene ends (see cutscenePreviewZoomPercent).
018887:         const cutsceneZoomMul = cutscenePreviewActive ? 100 / (cutscenePreviewZoomPercent || 100) : 1;
018888:         const tx = camTargetX, tz = camTargetZ;
018889:         // Cutscene/dialogue/portrait framing is deliberately scripted — only
018890:         // clamp the ordinary gameplay camera against tree canopies.
018891:         let effectiveZoomScale = s_zoomScale;
018892:         if (!cutscenePreviewActive && !dialogueZoomActive()) {
018893:           const approxLookY = camTargetY + (modeCfg.targetYOffsetTiles ?? 0);
018894:           const floor = canopyZoomFloor(tx, tz, approxLookY);
018895:           if (floor > effectiveZoomScale) {
018896:             const cfg = desktopControlsConfig();
018897:             const max = Number.isFinite(Number(cfg.wheelZoomMax)) ? Number(cfg.wheelZoomMax) : 2.5;
018898:             effectiveZoomScale = Math.min(floor, max);
018899:           }
018900:         }
018901:         const baseDistance = (modeCfg.distanceTiles ?? 14) / effectiveZoomScale * cutsceneZoomMul;
018902:         const distance = dialogueZoomActive() ? baseDistance / dialogueZoomFactor() : baseDistance;
018903:         const angle = THREE.MathUtils.degToRad((modeCfg.angleFromGroundDeg ?? 32.73) + cameraAngleOffsetDeg);
018904:         const azimuth = THREE.MathUtils.degToRad((modeCfg.azimuthDeg ?? 0) + cameraAzimuthOffsetDeg);
018905:         const portraitAim = dialoguePortraitCameraAim(modeCfg, tx, tz, distance, angle);
018906:         let lookY = portraitAim?.lookY ?? (camTargetY + (modeCfg.targetYOffsetTiles ?? 0));
018907:         // Camera sits at `azimuth` east of due-south from the target, elevated,
018908:         // looking back at it. azimuth=0 (every mode but "fishing") reduces to the
018909:         // original due-south-looking-north framing.
018910:         let lookAtX = portraitAim?.targetX ?? tx, lookAtZ = portraitAim?.targetZ ?? tz;
018911:         // Shoulder-surf's horizontal/vertical camera-offset sliders (Settings
018912:         // → Camera), applied relative to the camera's own right/world-up axes
018913:         // — the same over-the-shoulder framing knobs most third-person games
018914:         // expose — so they stay "camera-left/right" and "higher/lower"
018915:         // regardless of which way the head/camera currently points. Shifting
018916:         // the look-at point here (rather than the final camera position
018917:         // directly) carries the offset into idealX/idealZ/cameraY below too,
018918:         // sliding the whole camera rig rather than just skewing its aim.
018919:         if (activeCameraMode === SHOULDER_SURF_MODE && !portraitAim) {
018920:           const rightX = Math.cos(azimuth), rightZ = -Math.sin(azimuth);
018921:           lookAtX += rightX * s_shoulderSurfOffsetH_current;
018922:           lookAtZ += rightZ * s_shoulderSurfOffsetH_current;
018923:           lookY += s_shoulderSurfOffsetV_current;
018924:         }
018925:         const cameraY = portraitAim?.cameraY ?? (lookY + Math.sin(angle) * distance);
018926:         const groundDistance = Math.cos(angle) * distance;
018927:         const idealX = lookAtX + Math.sin(azimuth) * groundDistance;
018928:         const idealZ = lookAtZ + Math.cos(azimuth) * groundDistance; // +Z = south
018929:         const safe = occlusionSafeCameraPosition(lookAtX, lookY, lookAtZ, idealX, cameraY, idealZ);
018930:         camera.position.set(safe.x, safe.y, safe.z);
018931:         camera.lookAt(lookAtX, lookY, lookAtZ);
018932:         camera.fov = modeCfg.fovDeg ?? 42;
018933:         camera.aspect = threeContainer.clientWidth / threeContainer.clientHeight;
018934:         camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
018935:       }
018936:       updateCameraPosition();

018938:       // Camera-aligned view-corridor culling for dense zone vegetation — ports
018939:       // the standalone foliage tool's updateForestGeometryCulling. Toggling
018940:       // .visible on whole tree/bush/stump groups (bounding sphere precomputed
018941:       // once at build time, see cullSphere tagging in _buildZoneFloorMeshes)
018942:       // is far cheaper than every one of those groups' own per-object frustum
018943:       // test every single frame, and this corridor can hide far more than
018944:       // default frustum culling would (behind camera, wide off to the sides)
018945:       // — the "1-2 tile gaps throughout" density this exists to support can
018946:       // put thousands of these groups in one zone.
018947:       const VEG_CULL_FORWARD_TILES = 42;
018948:       const VEG_CULL_WIDTH_TILES = 30;
018949:       const VEG_CULL_REAR_TILES = 2;
018950:       const VEG_CULL_HYSTERESIS_TILES = 1;
018951:       let _vegCullAccum = 999; // force a real pass on the first tick
018952: 
018953:       // Keep the player (and anyone/anything else) visible when foliage is
018954:       // between them and the camera. A tree flagged as blocking the
018955:       // camera-player sightline (below, via isBetweenCameraAndPlayer2D)
018956:       // fades its own opacity down — but a transparent object with
018957:       // depthWrite left at its default (true) still writes full depth, so
018958:       // whatever's behind it still fails the depth test and gets fully
018959:       // occluded despite the tree visually reading as see-through. That
018960:       // asymmetry (tools showing through, characters not) was originally
018961:       // patched around with a "ghost" duplicate of the avatar/tool plane,
018962:       // stencil-gated to draw only behind a flagged-blocking tree — real,
018963:       // but a bandaid: it needed its own mesh built per revealable target
018964:       // (player, companion, mount, each tool, each hat swap) at avatar-build
018965:       // time, its own per-frame transform resync for anything that animates
018966:       // its own local transform after ghost creation (see the old
018967:       // updateToolMesh spinPlane note), and a wilderness-zone visibility
018968:       // gate — all just to work around one flag on the actual occluder.

018970:       // occlusion at its source instead: the tree stops writing depth for

018950:       const VEG_CULL_HYSTERESIS_TILES = 1;
018951:       let _vegCullAccum = 999; // force a real pass on the first tick
018952: 
018953:       // Keep the player (and anyone/anything else) visible when foliage is
018954:       // between them and the camera. A tree flagged as blocking the
018955:       // camera-player sightline (below, via isBetweenCameraAndPlayer2D)
018956:       // fades its own opacity down — but a transparent object with
018957:       // depthWrite left at its default (true) still writes full depth, so
018958:       // whatever's behind it still fails the depth test and gets fully
018959:       // occluded despite the tree visually reading as see-through. That
018960:       // asymmetry (tools showing through, characters not) was originally
018961:       // patched around with a "ghost" duplicate of the avatar/tool plane,
018962:       // stencil-gated to draw only behind a flagged-blocking tree — real,
018963:       // but a bandaid: it needed its own mesh built per revealable target
018964:       // (player, companion, mount, each tool, each hat swap) at avatar-build
018965:       // time, its own per-frame transform resync for anything that animates
018966:       // its own local transform after ghost creation (see the old
018967:       // updateToolMesh spinPlane note), and a wilderness-zone visibility
018968:       // gate — all just to work around one flag on the actual occluder.
018969:       // Dropping depthWrite once a tree is actually fading removes the
018970:       // occlusion at its source instead: the tree stops writing depth for
018971:       // exactly as long as it's actually transparent, so ANYTHING behind it
018972:       // (player, companion, wild animal, a bandit's weapon, whatever) shows
018973:       // through via ordinary alpha blending — no per-target ghost mesh, no
018974:       // stencil buffer, nothing to keep in sync each frame.
018975:       const TREE_FADE_OPACITY = 0.25;
018976:       const TREE_FADE_LERP_PER_SEC = 6;
018977:       // Sideways tolerance for the camera-player occlusion line test, as a
018978:       // fraction of a tree's own horizontal footprint radius (cullSphere's
018979:       // xzRadius) — halved from the full footprint so only trees whose trunk
018980:       // is genuinely close to dead-center on the sightline count as
018981:       // blocking, not merely anything within a whole canopy-width of it.
018982:       const OCCLUSION_XZ_RADIUS_MUL = 0.5;
018983:       const _treeFadeActive = new Set(); // vegGroup refs currently mid-fade
018984:       function ensureTreeFadeMaterials(vegGroup) {
018985:         let mats = vegGroup.userData._fadeMaterials;
018986:         if (mats) return mats;
018987:         mats = [];
018988:         for (const child of vegGroup.children) {
018989:           if (!child.material) continue;
018990:           const clone = child.material.clone();
018991:           clone.transparent = true;
018992:           child.material = clone;
018993:           mats.push(clone);
018994:         }
